findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the seam-internal enumeration: `_store/lock.py` contains no git (pure fcntl/mkdir lock — grep 'git' returns nothing), so remove it from the list of internals that 'issue raw git' / receive a `# raw-git-ok` marker, or replace it with the file that actually holds the lock-scoped raw git.
evidence: Grep of src/rebar/_store/lock.py for 'git' -> no matches; for 'subprocess' -> no matches.
lock.py docstring (lines 1-24) describes it as 'The ONE write lock' implemented via 'fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)' + 'mkdir lock' — a pure file lock, not a git caller.
Plan text: 'the store seam — locked write transactions ... whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git (... _store/lock.py, ...)'.
findings.finding: The plan enumerates src/rebar/_store/lock.py as a store-seam internal whose 'INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git' and lists it among the files to receive a `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker, but lock.py issues no git at all.
findings.location: Context/Problem + Scope: '_store/lock.py' listed under 'the store seam ... whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git'; Scope bullet 'inline markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, ...)'
scenarios: First-scan marker pass: author tries to add `# raw-git-ok` to lock.py and finds no raw git line to mark, wasting effort or mis-marking an unrelated line.
Reviewer at landing checks 'all enumerated seam internals are marked' and finds lock.py has no marker because there is nothing to mark, creating a false discrepancy against the AC.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop _store/lock.py from the raw-git seam-internal list; the lock-held raw git actually lives in _store/event_append.py (_run_git) and _commands/purge_bridge.py, which are already enumerated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Layer P's detection model with the code: the enumerated seam internals (txn.py, git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, event_append.py) route git through run_git/run_git_write/_run_git/_git wrappers (0 literal `subprocess.run(['git', <verb>])`), so specify whether Layer P also flags those wrapper calls — otherwise their `# raw-git-ok` markers are dead and wrapper-routed bypasses go undetected.
evidence: _commands/txn.py: grep 'subprocess.run' -> no matches; its `_git` helper (line 128) calls `run_git_write(tracker_dir, *args)`, i.e. add/commit go through the wrapper, not subprocess.
_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py: grep 'subprocess.run' -> no matches; add (231), update_ref (228), commit-tree (203) all delegate to `run_git(...)`.
_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py: update-ref CAS ops (370/459/488/542) go through a local `_git(repo_root, [...])` wrapper, not literal subprocess.run(['git',...]).

_store/event_append.py: `_run_git(argv)` (line 256) calls `subprocess.run(argv, ...)` where argv is a VARIABLE; the literal 'git'+verb lists (add/commit/rm at 277/299/314) are arguments to `_run_git`, not to subprocess.run — an argv-literal AST scan on subprocess calls would not see them.

By contrast the literal-argv sites purge_bridge.py:153-168, eval_solver.py:32-44, criterion_preview.py:414-415 DO call subprocess.run(['git', <verb>, ...]) and would be flagged — confirming the split.
gitutil.py:239-260 confirms run_git_write wraps run_git (the base subprocess shape), so mutations are one indirection removed from subprocess.run at the seam-internal call sites.
findings.finding: Layer P's stated detection rule ('flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb') cannot flag most of the enumerated seam internals it directs authors to mark, because they route git through wrapper functions (run_git / run_git_write / _run_git / _git), not literal subprocess.run(['git', <verb>, ...]) calls. The premise that 'every raw mutation ... ALL of them get flagged by default' is refuted for those files.
findings.location: Approach, Layer P: 'flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb ... UNLESS the line or enclosing function carries the marker'; and 'every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass. ALL of them get flagged by default'
scenarios: Author marks git_adapter/_ref_lock/event_append/txn per the Scope bullet, but Layer P never flags those lines, so the markers are dead and the lint provides no protection against a future raw wrapper-routed mutation there.

A NEW bypass added via `run_git_write(tracker, 'add', ...)` or `_run_git(['git', ..., 'commit', ...])` sails past Layer P because the scan keys on subprocess calls with literal 'git'+verb argv, which these do not present.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend Layer P to treat calls to the known git-execution wrappers (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git) whose first/argv element carries a mutation verb as raw-git mutations too, in addition to direct subprocess.run(['git',...]); then re-derive which enumerated files actually get flagged vs marked.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether _store/lock.py actually issues a flagged git mutation verb; if not, drop it from the enumerated marker list (its callers txn/event_append/purge_bridge carry the raw writes).
evidence: Plan: 'the store seam ... whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py run_git_write itself, _store/lock.py, _store/event_append.py's own _run_git ...)'
src/rebar/_store/lock.py docstring: 'fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) ... then the mkdir lock' — no git subprocess in the lock primitive
Scope lists markers 'on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, ...)'
findings.finding: The plan lists src/rebar/_store/lock.py among the seam INTERNALS that 'legitimately issue raw git' and therefore need a `# raw-git-ok:` marker, but lock.py is implemented with fcntl+mkdir and issues no git mutation verb, so Layer P would find nothing there to mark — the marker target does not exist in that file.
findings.location: Context/Problem and Scope — enumerated seam internals include '_store/lock.py'
scenarios: First scan applies markers to the enumerated list: lock.py has no flagged git op, so a marker there is dead/unneeeded and may confuse a reviewer expecting a git write in the lock primitive

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how Layer P handles git issued via the shared wrappers (run_git / run_git_write / _run_git / _git): either resolve those wrapper calls and flag a mutation verb threaded as a positional/list-fragment arg (not only literal `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`), or explicitly scope the rule and justify the exclusion.
evidence: git_adapter.py:225 `args = ["update-ref", ref, new_value]` then `run_git(_root(repo_root), *args)` — verb via wrapper, no literal 'git' argv
git_adapter.py:233 `run_git(_root(repo_root), "add", *paths)`
_ref_lock.py:459 `_git(repo_root, ["update-ref", ref, oid, _ZERO_OID], ...)`; :488/:542/:370 same shape
event_append.py:277/300 route the literal ['git',...] through `_run_git(argv)`; txn.py:128 `run_git_write(tracker_dir, *args)`
Plan text: 'flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb'
findings.finding: Layer P's detection rule ('flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb') does not match the actual call shape of the seam internals the plan says to mark, nor of most codebase git writes: git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, event_append.py and txn.py issue git through the shared wrappers run_git/run_git_write/_run_git/_git, where the mutation verb is threaded as a positional/list-fragment arg and the literal 'git' token lives inside the wrapper — not in a subprocess.run(['git', ...]) argv at the call site.
scenarios: A new bypass author writes `run_git(root, "commit", ...)` or `run_git_write(tracker, *["add","-A"])` from an unsanctioned module — Layer P as specified does not flag it because the literal 'git' argv shape is absent
The required markers on git_adapter.py/_ref_lock.py are inert because nothing at those lines matches the rule
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Layer P detector to recognize the codebase's git wrapper call-shape — flag a call to subprocess.run/Popen OR to run_git/run_git_write/_run_git/_git whose first git-arg (after cwd) is a mutation verb, resolving list-literal fragments (e.g. args = ["update-ref", ...]) — and place the required seam-internal markers on those wrapper call sites accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate ALL disposable-workspace raw-git sites that hit a flagged verb — add gerrit_client.py:374 (`git checkout`) and opcert_service/workspace.py:108/:125 (`git checkout`/`worktree add`) to the first-scan marker list (or explicitly fold them into the catch-all), and correct the 'two known sites' claim.
evidence: Plan: 'rebar's Python writes git only for the tracker/its mirrors OR for DISPOSABLE SANDBOX repos (two known sites: ...eval_solver.py..., ...criterion_preview.py...)'
src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:374 `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", dest, "checkout", "-q", "FETCH_HEAD"], ...)` — flagged verb `checkout` against an ephemeral mkdtemp clone
src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:108 `_git_ok(root, "checkout", "-q", "-B", cfg.review_branch, ...)` and :125 `_git_ok(root, "worktree", "add", ...)` against a tempfile.mkdtemp workspace
Plan verb list: 'add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean' — includes checkout
findings.finding: The plan claims raw-git disposable-sandbox writes have exactly 'two known sites' (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py), but at least two more Python sites issue a FLAGGED mutation verb (checkout) against disposable clone workspaces and are not enumerated: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:374 (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD`) and src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:108 (`git checkout -q -B ...`) plus :125 (`git worktree add`). Layer P (module-agnostic) WILL flag these, so they must be marked or remediated, but they are absent from the first-scan marker list.
findings.location: Approach — 'two known sites' rationale; Scope — inline marker enumeration; Testing — 'Full-tree run is clean at merge'
scenarios: First full scan runs Layer P: gerrit_client.py:374 and workspace.py:108 fire the lint but carry no marker and are not in the enumerated first-scan list → tree is NOT clean at merge unless they are found and marked/remediated ad hoc
A reviewer relying on the plan's 'two known sites' claim to size the marker work under-counts the disposable-repo category
findings.suggested_fix: Rescope the sandbox enumeration to name eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py, and opcert_service/workspace.py (the `_git`/`_git_ok` wrapper functions), each getting `# raw-git-ok: disposable clone/workspace, not the tracker`; replace 'two known sites' with the accurate count.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the seam-internal marker inventory from a full symbol/grep sweep of git mutation verbs across src/rebar (not the hand list): add delete.py, compact.py, and fsck_repair.py (their own `_git` add/commit/reset sites) to the enumerated marking targets, and either add a fourth Rationale category for provisioning-clone writers (opcert_service/workspace.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py) or explicitly route them to a marker reason, so the 'seam internal / sandbox / bypass' trichotomy holds.
evidence: Plan enumeration (Scope + Context): names only gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock as seam internals to mark.

Omitted seam internal: src/rebar/_commands/delete.py:326 `_git(tracker, "add", *staged)`, :353 `_git(tracker, "commit", ...)`, :360 bare `subprocess.run(["git","-C",tracker,"reset",...])` — locked store write via its own `_git` (delete.py:173).
Omitted seam internal: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:374/:553/:745 `_git(tracker, "add", "-A", ...)`, :381/:559/:751 `_git(tracker, "commit", ...)` — own `_git` (compact.py:58).
Omitted seam internal: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:346 `_git(tracker, "add", "-A")`, :353 `_git(tracker, "commit", ...)` — own `_git` (fsck_repair.py:56).

Rationale counter-example: src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:108 `checkout -q -B`, :125 `worktree add`, :106/:123 `remote add`; src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:389 `remote add` — raw mutations that are neither seam internal, sandbox fixture, nor tracker bypass, contradicting "every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass".
findings.finding: The Scope's committed inventory of seam internals to mark ("gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock") is incomplete: a codebase sweep for git mutation verbs finds several locked-store-write command internals with their own `_git()` wrappers that are neither enumerated nor covered by the named buckets — delete.py, compact.py, and fsck_repair.py. Each mutates the tracker under the write lock, so each will be flagged by Layer P and must carry a `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` marker, but none is named as a marking target. The plan's Rationale further asserts "every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass", yet opcert_service/workspace.py and review_bot/gerrit_client.py issue raw mutations (worktree/remote add, checkout) that fit none of the three categories.
findings.location: Scope: "inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)"
scenarios: delete.py add/commit/reset (:326/:353/:360): unmarked at landing → Layer P flags them and the "tree is clean at landing" acceptance criterion fails, or they are marked ad hoc during the first scan without being named in Scope (silent under-delivery of the enumerated deliverable).
compact.py six add/commit sites and fsck_repair.py add/commit: same — flagged by Layer P, absent from the committed marker list.

opcert_service/workspace.py and gerrit_client.py raw mutations: flagged by Layer P (module-agnostic) but the Rationale offers no category for them, so the marker reason to apply is undefined and the 'every mutation is seam/sandbox/bypass' claim is falsified.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, expand the enumerated seam-internals list to include _commands/delete.py, _commands/compact.py, and _commands/fsck_repair.py (each mutates the tracker under the write lock via its own `_git`). In the Rationale, add a fourth category for ephemeral workspace provisioning (opcert_service/workspace.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py `remote add`/`worktree add`/`checkout`) with its own marker reason, or explicitly classify those as disposable-clone sandbox writes.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: Two acceptance-criteria claims are documentation/prose claims (AC2 'relationship to the existing tickets-boundary-ok convention documented'; AC4 'the variable-indirection residual documented in the lint header') but the Testing section provides no proving check that these texts actually exist — the unit tests only exercise the P/W flagging behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the chosen mutation-verb set explicitly and justify inclusions/exclusions (e.g. add commit-tree and push-to-ref, or record why they are out of scope), so the verb list is not silently under-inclusive of the reconciler's write shape.
evidence: git_adapter.py:205 uses verb 'commit-tree' (not in the plan's list; distinct from 'commit')
_ref_lock.py references `git push origin :<ref>` and update-ref CAS as the two write halves
Plan verb list: 'add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean'
findings.finding: The Layer P mutation-verb set (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean) omits write verbs the reconciler/store actually use — notably `commit-tree` (git_adapter.commit_tree) and `push` to TICKETS_REF (_ref_lock CAS) — with no stated rationale for the chosen set.
scenarios: A new write via `run_git(root, "commit-tree", ...)` + `update-ref` (the reconciler's own commit shape) partially escapes because commit-tree is not a flagged verb

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the Layer P static residual (verbs/tracker paths passed as variables or routed through git wrappers) in the lint header and docs, symmetric to the stated Layer W residual, so the coverage boundary is explicit.
evidence: Plan documents only the Layer W residual: 'tracker targeting laundered through a variable is undetectable statically'
No corresponding Layer P residual is stated, yet run_git_write(tracker_dir, *args) (txn.py:128) and git_adapter update_ref's `run_git(root, *args)` pass verbs as non-literals
findings.finding: The plan documents the Layer W static residual (tracker targeting laundered through a variable) but states no equivalent residual for Layer P. Because much of the codebase issues git through wrappers with verbs passed as *args/variables, verb-via-variable and wrapper-routed writes are an undocumented Layer P blind spot.
scenarios: A reviewer or author assumes Layer P catches all rebar Python raw writes; a wrapper-routed or verb-in-variable write passes silently

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the lint's behavior on unparseable files (fail-closed with a clear message vs skip-and-warn) for Python AST, YAML, and shell inputs.
evidence: 'Layer P (Python, AST): parse src/rebar/**/*.py + scripts/*.py'
'Layer W ... parse .github/workflows/*.yml run-blocks and scripts/*.sh'
Absence: no stated fail-open vs fail-closed behavior for unparseable inputs
findings.finding: The lint reads and parses Python (AST), YAML, and shell files, but the plan does not state how it behaves when a file fails to parse (a syntax error, malformed YAML run-block, or unparseable shell). A CI gate that crashes on a malformed file, or silently skips it, could either block unrelated work or let a bypass through unflagged.
findings.location: Approach (Layer P AST parse / Layer W parse of run-blocks); Scope (new lint script)
scenarios: A workflow YAML with a syntax error reaches CI and the lint step raises an unhandled exception instead of a teaching failure
A Python file with a parse error is silently skipped, hiding a raw git write inside it
findings.suggested_fix: Specify fail-closed: on a parse error, emit the file path and a clear error and exit non-zero, so a malformed file cannot silently hide a bypass.

findings.finding: Layer P's load-bearing rationale ('rebar's Python writes git ONLY for the tracker or its mirrors, so every raw mutation is either a seam internal or a bypass') is factually false: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py and src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py run raw subprocess git add/commit/checkout against disposable, non-tracker sandbox repos (eval fixtures / detector-preview tempdirs). These are legitimate git writes that are neither seam-internal nor bypasses, yet Layer P (module-agnostic, in scope src/rebar/**/*.py) will flag them, forcing spurious '# raw-git-ok' markers that mislabel unrelated code as store-write-seam-internal.
findings.location: Approach — 'Rationale for module-agnostic flagging'; Scope — Layer P scan of src/rebar/**/*.py
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) exclude src/rebar/llm/evals and src/rebar/llm/workflow (or the preview/eval sandbox helpers) from Layer P's scan, or (b) explicitly enumerate eval_solver.py and criterion_preview.py in the first-scan remediation list with a marker reason that names them as disposable non-tracker fixture repos — and revise the Approach rationale to acknowledge non-tracker sandbox git writes rather than asserting rebar Python writes git ONLY for the tracker.
